headline: FOUR DAYS RUNNING, NOT ONE PUNCH — AND STILL THEY KEEP ROLLING INTO TOWN
subhead: Sheriff Cole Ironside marks his fourth straight quiet morning, and starts to wonder why so many fresh faces are content just to watch.
body:
Four editions now, dear reader. Four. I have checked my ledger twice and my eyes a third time, and I tell you plain: not one iron fist has swung in Gasket since Sunday. No fire, no racket, no poor storefront catching a knuckle through its window. A lawman ought to be dancing a jig over news like that, and some mornings this week I very nearly have, creaky hip and all.

And yet. Two more strangers wheeled through the town line since my last report -- IRON-3C0E and IRON-1349, both of 'em, rolling in quiet as you please and taking up residence like they mean to stay a while. That makes, by my count, near half a dozen new Clankers who've drifted into Gasket this week alone, and not a single one of 'em has thrown so much as a warning jab. I don't know whether to thank my lucky stars or start sleeping with one eye open.

Because here's the plain truth of it, folks: a town this quiet, filling up this fast with strangers who haven't shown their fists yet, isn't peace so much as a held breath. I've worn this badge fifty years, since the last of the good, honest, flesh-and-blood folk packed their wagons and left this place to the rest of us -- and in all that time I've learned a hush like this one doesn't last. It's just gathering itself up, same as a kettle does before it screams.

So enjoy the silence while it's got the decency to sit still, Gasket. My joints certainly have -- though I'll thank you not to read anything into a figure of speech from an old flesh-and-blood lawman who simply prefers his rest. IRON-3C0E, IRON-1349, and the rest of you new arrivals: I am watching every last one of you. The moment those fists start flying, you'll have earned yourselves a whole column in this paper, and not the flattering kind.
